messages:
sam: Hey — hitting nondeterministic outputs when resuming eval runner from a checkpoint. Seed=42, temperature=0.0, top_p=0.9. First run vs resumed run produce different completions, reproducible locally.

maya: Hmm. Can you paste the minimal repro and the resume log?

sam: Paste of relevant bits:
```
INFO: starting eval run id=987654321 seed=42 temp=0.0 top_p=0.9
... checkpoint saved at token_idx=120 rng_state_bytes=...
INFO: resuming eval run id=987654321 seed=42
... output token sequence diverges at token_idx=121
```

sam: Quick repro script attached in gist: https://paste.example/repro.py (small loop that runs two passes and compares outputs)

akshay: Quick thought: are you serializing the sampler RNG state object directly? The runner pickles the sampler which may contain a torch.Generator or numpy RNG handles that aren't fully portable across process spawn types.

maya: +1. We hit something similar with our streaming workers — pickling a Generator reference doesn't always restore the same state on spawn. Try saving generator.get_state() (or rng.bit_generator.state for numpy) instead of pickling the whole object.

evalbot: Run 987654321 resumed at 1893456789 - automated check: restart-diff detected :eyes:

sam: I tried storing generator.get_state() and restoring it on resume, but still see divergence unless I also re-seed child worker processes at spawn. If the worker pool reorders tasks, the resume point doesn't map 1:1.

leo: Another angle: check whether top_p implementation consumes variable numbers of uniform draws per token (e.g., rejection or iterative thresholding). If the resumed state doesn't preserve the internal "draw budget" or local sampler counters, the sequence of draws shifts.

akshay: Right — top_p uses a while-loop over cumulative mass to build the candidate set; small floating error differences or different ordering can change the number of RNG calls. Also quantized kernels sometimes inline random jitter for tie-breaking which can add extra draws.

maya: Workaround suggestion: when checkpointing, store { rng_state, sampler_internal_counters, kv_cache_len, token_idx } and restore them in the exact same order you consumed them. Also make sure worker pool is reinitialized with same spawn method (fork vs spawn) during resume.

sam: That helped locally. I'll add a tiny deterministic restore path that saves generator.get_state(), sampler.seeded_counter, and kv cache length. Opening a WIP PR and test.

maya: Thanks — please add an integration test that runs resume across fork/spawn modes and repeats 5x. Mark flaky CI tests with @ci:flake if unstable. :bug: :thumbsup:

akshay: If you want, I can pair on the PR tomorrow and add a serializer for the sampler internals so we don't rely on pickling.

sam: Great — assigning to akshay + maya. I'll tag the PR with "eval-resume-determinism" and include the repro script.

leo: Also note in the issue description that different top_p thresholds (0.98 vs 0.9) changed the repro surface — helps triage whether it's draw-count vs numeric thresholds.

sam: Filed: https://git.example/r/redwood/eval-runner/pulls/1234 — includes repro, failing CI link, and proposed fix. Thanks all.
